title.zh: 卷一百三十二 列傳第十九: 杭忽思 步魯合答 玉哇失 麥里 探馬赤 拔都兒 昂吉兒 哈剌䚟 沙全 帖木兒不花
title.en: Volume 132 Biographies 19: Hanghusi, Buluheda, Yuwashi, Maili, Tanmachi, Badou'er, Angji'er, Haladai, Sha Quan, Tiemu'erbuhua
title.raw: 卷一百三十二 列傳第十九: 杭忽思 步魯合答 玉哇失 麥里 探馬赤 拔都兒 昂吉兒 哈剌䚟 沙全 帖木兒不花 Volume 132 Biographies 19: Hanghusi, Buluheda, Yuwashi, Maili, Tanmachi, Badou'er, Angji'er, Haladai, Sha Quan, Tiemu'erbuhua

sentences.zh: 杭忽思

translations.literal: Hanghusi
translations.idiomatic: Hanghusi

sentences.zh: 杭忽思，阿速氏，主阿速國。

translations.literal: Hanghusi was of the Asud clan and ruled the kingdom of the Asud.
translations.idiomatic: Hanghusi belonged to the Asud people and held sway over their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 太宗兵至其境，杭忽思率衆來降，賜名拔都兒，錫以金符，命領其土民。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong's army reached his territory, Hanghusi led the multitude to submit. He was granted the name Badou'er, bestowed a gold tally, and ordered to govern his native people.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong's forces reached his lands, Hanghusi led his people in surrender. He received the name Badou'er, a gold tally, and command over his own subjects.

sentences.zh: 尋奉旨選阿速軍千人，及其長子阿塔赤扈駕親征。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he received an edict to select a thousand Asud troops, and his eldest son Atachi accompanied the emperor on a personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to muster a thousand Asud soldiers, and his eldest son Atachi joined the emperor's personal expedition.

sentences.zh: 既還，阿塔赤入直宿衛。

translations.literal: After their return, Atachi entered regular palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, Atachi was posted to the palace guard on regular rotation.

sentences.zh: 杭忽思還國，道遇敵人，戰歿，敕其妻外麻思領兵守其國。

translations.literal: Hanghusi returned to his country, met enemies on the road, and died in battle. An edict ordered his wife Waimasi to lead troops and defend the country.
translations.idiomatic: Hanghusi was homeward bound when he met foes on the road and fell in battle. The court commanded his wife Waimasi to take the army and hold the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 外麻思躬擐甲冑，平叛亂，後以次子按法普代之。

translations.literal: Waimasi personally donned armor, suppressed rebellions, and later her second son Anfapu replaced her.
translations.idiomatic: Waimasi herself buckled on armor and put down revolts; later her second son Anfapu took her place.

sentences.zh: 阿塔赤從憲宗征西川軍于釣魚山，與宋兵戰有功，帝親飲以酒，賞以白金。

translations.literal: Atachi followed Emperor Xianzong in campaigning against western Sichuan; the army was at Diaoyushan. He fought the Song with merit; the emperor personally gave him wine to drink and rewarded him with white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Atachi marched with Xianzong against western Sichuan and fought at Diaoyushan, where he distinguished himself against the Song. The emperor drank with him in person and gave him white gold.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥叛，從也里可征之，至寧夏，與阿藍荅兒、渾都海戰，率先赴敵，矢中其腹，不懼，世祖聞而嘉之，賞以白金，召入宿衛。

translations.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he followed Yelikhe in campaigning against him. At Ningxia he fought Arigh Böke and Qutuqai, took the lead rushing at the enemy, was struck in the belly by an arrow but did not fear. Emperor Shizu heard and praised him, rewarded white gold, and summoned him into palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: During Ariq Böke's revolt he campaigned under Yelikhe as far as Ningxia, where he battled Arigh Böke and Qutuqai, charging ahead though an arrow pierced his belly. Kublai praised his courage, gave him white gold, and brought him into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，扈駕親征阿里不哥，追至失木里禿之地，以功復賞白金。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he accompanied the emperor on a personal campaign against Ariq Böke, pursued to the place of Shimulitu, and was again rewarded with white gold for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 he joined the emperor's personal campaign against Ariq Böke, pursuing him to Shimulitu, and received another grant of white gold for his service.

sentences.zh: 三年，從征李璮，平之。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed the campaign against Li Tan and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he took part in the campaign against Li Tan and helped bring it to an end.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，奉旨同不荅台領兵南征，攻破金剛臺。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan, by imperial order he joined Badutai in leading troops south, capturing the Jingang Platform.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 he was ordered south with Badutai and helped storm the Jingang Platform.

sentences.zh: 六年，從攻安慶府，戰有功。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the attack on Anqing Prefecture and fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he fought at Anqing Prefecture and again distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 七年，從下五河口。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed in reducing the Wuhekou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he helped take the Wuhekou.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從下沿江諸郡，戍鎮巢，民不堪命，宋降將洪福以計乘醉而殺之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed in reducing the prefectures along the Yangtze, garrisoned Zhenchao. The people could not bear the burdens; the Song surrender general Hong Fu used a stratagem to kill him while he was drunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he helped subdue the Yangtze prefectures and was posted to garrison Zhenchao, where the people groaned under harsh rule. The surrendered Song officer Hong Fu tricked him into a feast and killed him while he was drunk.

sentences.zh: 世祖憫其死，賜其家白金五百兩、鈔三千五百貫，併鎮巢降民一千五百三十九戶，且命其子伯荅兒襲千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu pitied his death, gave his family five hundred taels of white gold and three thousand five hundred strings of paper money, together with one thousand five hundred thirty-nine surrendered households of Zhenchao, and ordered his son Bada'er to inherit the chiliarch post, wearing the gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai mourned his death and granted his household five hundred taels of white gold, three thousand five hundred strings of paper money, and the 1,539 surrendered households of Zhenchao. He also had his son Bada'er inherit the chiliarchy with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 時失烈吉叛，詔伯荅兒領阿速軍一千往征之，與甕吉剌只兒瓦台軍戰于押里，復與藥木忽兒軍戰于禿剌及斡魯歡之地。

translations.literal: At that time Shilieji rebelled. An edict ordered Bada'er to lead a thousand Asud troops to campaign against him. He fought the army of Onggirad Jirwatai at Yali, and again fought the army of Yeshmutu'er at Tula and at Olughun.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilieji rose in revolt, Bada'er was ordered to take a thousand Asud troops against him. He fought Jirwatai of the Onggirad at Yali, then clashed with Yeshmutu'er's forces at Tula and Olughun.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，至伯牙之地，與赤憐軍合戰。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifteenth year he reached the place of Boya and joined battle with the Chiling army.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifteenth year he reached Boya and fought the Chiling forces.

sentences.zh: 五月，駐兵呵剌牙，與外剌台、寬赤哥思等軍合戰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he encamped at Halaya and joined battle with the armies of Walatai, Kuanchiges, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he camped at Halaya and fought Walatai, Kuanchiges, and their allies.

sentences.zh: 其大將塔思不花樹木為柵，積石為城，以拒大軍。

translations.literal: Their general Tasibuhua erected trees as palisades and piled stones as walls to resist the great army.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Tasibuhua built wooden palisades and stone walls to hold off the main force.

sentences.zh: 伯荅兒督勇士先登，拔之，伯荅兒矢中右股，別吉里迷失以其功聞，賞白金。

translations.literal: Bada'er urged the brave men to climb first, captured it, and was struck by an arrow in the right thigh. Begirimishi reported his merit, and he was rewarded with white gold.
translations.idiomatic: Bada'er drove his men to scale the works first and took them, though an arrow struck his right thigh. Begirimishi reported his feat and he was given white gold.

sentences.zh: 二十年，授虎符、定遠大將軍、後衛親軍都指揮使，兼領阿速軍，充阿速拔都達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was granted a tiger tally, made General for Pacifying the Distant, Commander-in-Chief of the Rear Guard Personal Army, concurrently commanding the Asud army, and appointed darughachi of the Asud Badu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he received a tiger tally and the posts of general for pacifying the distant and commander of the rear guard personal army, while continuing to lead the Asud troops as their badu darughachi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，征別失八里，軍于亦里渾察罕兒之地，與禿呵、不早麻軍戰，有功。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he campaigned against Beshbaligh, encamped at Yilihun Chaghan'er, fought the armies of Tuqa and Buzama, and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he marched on Beshbaligh, camped at Yilihun Chaghan'er, and distinguished himself against the forces of Tuqa and Buzama.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，征杭海，敵勢甚盛，大軍乏食，其母乃咬真輸己帑及畜牧等給軍食，世祖聞而嘉之，賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he campaigned against Hanghai. The enemy's strength was very great and the great army lacked food. His mother Naiyaozhen contributed her own stores and livestock to supply the army's food. Emperor Shizu heard and praised this, granting rewards very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, campaigning against Hanghai, the enemy was strong and supplies ran short. His mother Naiyaozhen gave her own treasury goods and herds to feed the troops. Kublai praised her and rewarded them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，伯荅兒卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, Bada'er died.
translations.idiomatic: Bada'er died in Dade 4.

sentences.zh: 長子斡羅思，由宿衛仕至隆鎮衛都指揮使；

translations.literal: The eldest son Woluosi, rising from palace guard service, reached the post of Commander-in-Chief of the Longzhen Guard;
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Woluosi rose from the palace guard to commander of the Longzhen Guard;

sentences.zh: 次子福定，襲職，官懷遠大將軍，尋改右阿速衛達魯花赤，兼管後衛軍。

translations.literal: The second son Fuding inherited the office, held the rank of General for Cherishing the Distant, and soon was changed to darughachi of the Right Asud Guard, concurrently managing the rear guard army.
translations.idiomatic: the second son Fuding inherited the post as general for cherishing the distant, soon became darughachi of the Right Asud Guard, and also oversaw the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，兄都丹充右阿速衛都指揮使；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhide, his elder brother Dudan served as Commander-in-Chief of the Right Asud Guard;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 4 his elder brother Dudan became commander of the Right Asud Guard;

sentences.zh: 福定復職後衛，陞樞密同僉，命領軍一千守遷民鎮，尋授定遠大將軍、僉樞密院事、後衛親軍都指揮使，提調右衛阿速達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Fuding resumed office in the rear guard, was promoted to Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, ordered to lead a thousand troops to garrison Qianmin Town, and soon was appointed General for Pacifying the Distant, Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Commander-in-Chief of the Rear Guard Personal Army, and supervisor of the Right Guard Asud darughachi.
translations.idiomatic: Fuding then returned to the rear guard, rose to associate commissioner of military affairs, and was sent with a thousand men to hold Qianmin Town. He was soon made general for pacifying the distant, associate commissioner, commander of the rear guard personal army, and overseer of the Right Guard Asud darughachi.

sentences.zh: 二年，進資善大夫、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Grand Master for Fostering Goodness and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was promoted to grand master for fostering goodness and vice commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 後至元間，進知樞密院事。

translations.literal: During the Houzhiyuan reign he was advanced to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hou Yuan he became commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 步魯合荅

translations.literal: Buluhecha
translations.idiomatic: Buluhecha

sentences.zh: 至元二年，車里以老疾，不任事，諸王阿只吉命步魯合荅代領其軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, Cheli was aged and ill and could not attend to affairs. Prince Azhi ordered Buluhecha to replace him in commanding the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 Cheli was too old and ill to serve, and Prince Azhi put Buluhecha in command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，制授管軍千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed by regulation as chiliarch in charge of troops, wearing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 8 he was formally made a troop chiliarch with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 宋將昝萬壽攻成都，僉省嚴忠範遣步魯合荅將兵七百人禦之于沙坎，流矢中右頰，拔矢，戰愈力，大敗其軍。

translations.literal: The Song general Zan Wanshou attacked Chengdu. Associate Secretariat Yan Zhongfan dispatched Buluhecha with seven hundred troops to resist him at Shakan. A stray arrow struck his right cheek; he pulled it out and fought with greater force, greatly defeating their army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Zan Wanshou threatened Chengdu, Yan Zhongfan sent Buluhecha with seven hundred men to hold Shakan. A stray arrow hit his right cheek; he pulled it out, fought harder, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，行院汪田哥以兵圍嘉定，步魯合荅即率其衆攻九頂山，破之，嘉定降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the mobile secretariat Wang Tiange besieged Jiading with troops. Buluhecha immediately led his forces to attack Jiuding Mountain, captured it, and Jiading surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Wang Tiange of the mobile secretariat besieged Jiading. Buluhecha stormed Jiuding Mountain, took it, and Jiading surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進攻重慶，宋軍突圍出走銅鑼峽，行院忽敦遣步魯合荅追之，至廣羊埧，斬首二百級。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Chongqing, the Song army broke out of encirclement and fled through Tongluo Gorge. The mobile secretariat Hudun dispatched Buluhecha to pursue them to Guangyangba and beheaded two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Chongqing the Song broke out toward Tongluo Gorge. Hudun sent Buluhecha in pursuit to Guangyangba, where he took two hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 瀘州叛，還軍討之，步魯合荅以所部兵攻寶子寨，歲餘不下，乃造雲梯先登，急擊，遂破之，殺虜殆盡。

translations.literal: Luzhou rebelled; the army returned to suppress it. Buluhecha with his division attacked Baozi Stockade. For more than a year it would not fall; he then built scaling ladders, climbed first, pressed the attack sharply, and finally captured it, killing and capturing nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou rebelled he marched back to crush it. His men besieged Baozi Stockade for over a year until he built siege ladders, led the climb, stormed the place, and slaughtered nearly everyone inside.

sentences.zh: 十六年，取重慶，以功遷武略將軍、征行元帥。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Chongqing was taken. For his merit he was transferred to General of Military Stratagem and campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Chongqing fell, and he was promoted to general of military stratagem and campaign marshal.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，命統蒙古探馬赤軍千人從征金齒蠻，平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was ordered to command a thousand Mongol tamachi troops in campaigning against the Jinchi barbarians, and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he led a thousand Mongol tamachi in the campaign against the Jinchi tribes and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 都元帥蒙古歹征羅必甸，步魯合荅率游兵先行，江水暴溢，率衆泅水而渡，去城三百步而營。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Mengudai campaigned against Luobidian. Buluhecha led vanguard troops ahead. The river water rose violently; he led the multitude to swim across and encamped three hundred paces from the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Mengudai marched on Luobidian, Buluhecha took the vanguard ahead. The river surged, but he swam his men across and pitched camp three hundred paces from the town.

sentences.zh: 居七日，諸軍會城下，乃進攻之，步魯合荅先登，拔其城，遂屠之。

translations.literal: After seven days the various armies assembled below the city and then advanced to attack it. Buluhecha climbed first, captured the city, and then slaughtered it.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later the armies gathered under the walls and assaulted the town. Buluhecha was first over the wall, took the city, and put it to the sword.

sentences.zh: 又從征八百媳婦國，至車厘，車厘者，其酋長所居也。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against the Babai Xifu country, reaching Cheli—Cheli being where their chieftain dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined the campaign against Babai Xifu and reached Cheli, the seat of their chieftain.

sentences.zh: 諸王闊闊命步魯合荅將游騎三百往招之降，不聽，進兵攻之，都鎮撫侯正死焉。

translations.literal: Prince Kuoku ordered Buluhecha to lead three hundred mounted scouts to summon their surrender; they would not listen. Advancing troops to attack, Regional Commander Hou Zheng died there.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuoku sent Buluhecha with three hundred light horsemen to demand surrender, but they refused. When the attack began, Regional Commander Hou Zheng was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 步魯合荅毀其北門木，遂入其寨，其地悉平。

translations.literal: Buluhecha destroyed the timber of their north gate, then entered their stockade, and the whole region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhecha smashed the north gate timbers, stormed the stockade, and pacified the whole district.

sentences.zh: 賜金虎符，授懷遠大將軍、雲南萬戶府達魯花赤，卒。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold tiger tally, appointed General for Cherishing the Distant and darughachi of the Yunnan Myriarchate, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He received a gold tiger tally and the posts of general for cherishing the distant and Yunnan myriarchate darughachi, then died.

sentences.zh: 子忙古不花，襲管軍千戶。

translations.literal: His son Mangubuhua inherited the chiliarch post in charge of troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mangubuhua inherited the troop chiliarchy.

sentences.zh: 初，按主奴三子：長車里，次黑子，次帖木兒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Anzhunu had three sons: the eldest Cheli, the second Heizi, and the third Timur.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhunu had three sons: Cheli the eldest, Heizi next, and Timur the youngest.

sentences.zh: 黑子別賜金符，為奧魯元帥，兼文州吐蕃達魯花赤，卒。

translations.literal: Heizi was separately granted a gold tally, made Ordu Marshal, and concurrently darughachi of the Tibetan region of Wenzhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Heizi received a separate gold tally as Ordu marshal and Wenzhou Tibetan darughachi before his death.

sentences.zh: 其子那懷幼，以帖木兒攝其官。

translations.literal: His son Nahuan was young; Timur acted in his stead in the office.
translations.idiomatic: While his son Nahuan was still a child, Timur held the post for him.

sentences.zh: 那懷長，解職授之，遂改授帖木兒隨路拔都萬戶，後移鎮重慶，卒。

translations.literal: When Nahuan grew up, the acting office was relinquished and given to him. Timur was then reassigned as route-wide Badu myriarch, later transferred to garrison Chongqing, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Nahuan came of age the office passed to him, and Timur was made route-wide Badu myriarch, later posted to Chongqing, where he died.

sentences.zh: 玉哇失

translations.literal: Yuwashi
translations.idiomatic: Yuwashi

sentences.zh: 玉哇失，阿速人。

translations.literal: Yuwashi was an Asud man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwashi was of the Asud people.

sentences.zh: 父也烈拔都兒，從其國主來歸，太宗命充宿衛。

translations.literal: His father Yeliebadou'er followed his country's ruler in coming to submit; Emperor Taizong ordered him to serve as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yeliebadou'er came with their king to submit, and Taizong enrolled him in the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，從憲宗征蜀，為游兵，前行至重慶，戰數有功。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu he followed Emperor Xianzong in campaigning against Shu as vanguard troops, advancing ahead to Chongqing, and fought with merit many times.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year he marched with Xianzong against Shu as a vanguard, reaching Chongqing ahead of the main force and winning repeated credit in battle.

sentences.zh: 嘗出獵遇虎於隘，下馬搏虎，虎張吻欲噬之，以手探虎口，抉其舌，拔所佩刀刺而殺之。

translations.literal: Once while out hunting he met a tiger in a narrow pass, dismounted to wrestle the tiger, the tiger opened its jaws wanting to devour him; he reached his hand into the tiger's mouth, pulled out its tongue, drew the knife at his belt and stabbed it to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a hunt he met a tiger in a narrow defile, dismounted, and fought it hand to hand. When it opened its jaws to bite him he thrust his hand into its mouth, seized its tongue, drew his belt knife, and killed it.

sentences.zh: 帝壯其勇，賞黃金五十兩，別立阿速一軍，使領其衆。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his bravery, rewarded fifty taels of yellow gold, and separately established an Asud army, making him lead its multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his courage, gave him fifty taels of gold, and formed a separate Asud corps under his command.

sentences.zh: 從世祖征阿里不哥，又從親王哈必失征李璮，俱有功，賜金符，授本軍千戶。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Shizu in campaigning against Ariq Böke, and again followed Prince Habishi in campaigning against Li Tan; in both he had merit, was granted a gold tally, and appointed chiliarch of his own army.
translations.idiomatic: He served Kublai against Ariq Böke and Prince Habishi against Li Tan, earning rewards each time, a gold tally, and the chiliarchy of his own unit.

sentences.zh: 從下襄陽，又從下沿江諸城，宋洪安撫既降復叛，誘其入城宴，乘醉殺之。

translations.literal: He followed in reducing Xiangyang, and again followed in reducing the cities along the Yangtze. The Song Hong pacification commissioner had surrendered then rebelled again, lured him into the city for a feast, and killed him while he was drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Xiangyang and the Yangtze towns. A surrendered Song pacification commissioner of the Hong clan feigned loyalty, invited him to a feast in the city, and killed him while he was drunk.

sentences.zh: 長子也速歹兒代領其軍，從攻揚州，中流矢卒。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yesudai'er replaced him in commanding the army, followed the attack on Yangzhou, was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yesudai'er took command and joined the assault on Yangzhou, where a stray arrow killed him.

sentences.zh: 玉哇失襲父職，為阿速軍千戶。

translations.literal: Yuwashi inherited his father's office as chiliarch of the Asud army.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwashi inherited his father's post as chiliarch of the Asud army.

sentences.zh: 從丞相伯顏平宋，賜巢縣二千五十二戶。

translations.literal: He followed Chancellor Bayan in pacifying the Song and was granted two thousand five hundred fifty-two households of Chaoxian County.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Chancellor Bayan to conquer the Song and was granted 2,552 households in Chaoxian County.

sentences.zh: 只兒瓦歹叛，率所部兵擊之，至懷魯哈都，擒其將失剌察兒，斬于軍，其衆悉平。

translations.literal: Jirwadai rebelled; he led his division to strike him, reaching Huailuhadu, captured his general Shilacha'er, beheaded him in the army, and pacified his forces entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Jirwadai rebelled he led his men to Huailuhadu, captured the rebel general Shilacha'er, executed him before the troops, and pacified the rest.

sentences.zh: 諸王和林及失剌等叛，從皇子北安王討之，至斡耳罕河，無舟，躍馬涉流而渡，俘獲甚衆。

translations.literal: Princes Helin and Shila and others rebelled; he followed the prince Northern Pacification King to suppress them. Reaching the Orkhon River with no boats, he leaped his horse through the current to cross and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: When Princes Helin, Shila, and others rose in revolt he campaigned with the Northern Pacification Prince to the Orkhon. With no boats he spurred his horse through the current and took many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時北安王方戰失利，陷敵陣中，玉哇失從諸王藥木忽兒追至金山，王乃得脫歸。

translations.literal: At that time the Northern Pacification King was fighting with defeat and trapped in the enemy formation. Yuwashi followed Prince Yeshmutu'er in pursuit to Jinshan, and the prince was thus able to escape and return.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Pacification Prince was then losing ground and trapped in the enemy lines. Yuwashi rode with Prince Yeshmutu'er to Jinshan and brought the prince safely out.

sentences.zh: 賞白金五十兩、鈔二千五百貫，改賜金虎符，進定遠大將軍、前衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: He was rewarded fifty taels of white gold and two thousand five hundred strings of paper money, granted a gold tiger tally in exchange, and advanced to General for Pacifying the Distant and Commander-in-Chief of the Forward Guard Personal Army.
translations.idiomatic: He received fifty taels of white gold and 2,500 strings of paper money, a gold tiger tally, and promotion to general for pacifying the distant and commander of the forward guard personal army.

sentences.zh: 諸王乃顏叛，世祖親征，玉哇失為前鋒。

translations.literal: Prince Nayiyan rebelled; Emperor Shizu personally campaigned, and Yuwashi served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Nayiyan rebelled, Kublai marched in person and Yuwashi led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 乃顏遣哈丹領兵萬人來拒，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Nayiyan dispatched Hadan to lead ten thousand troops to resist; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Nayiyan sent Hadan with ten thousand men to block him, and he routed them.

sentences.zh: 追至不里古都伯塔哈之地，乃顏兵號十萬，玉哇失陷陣力戰，又敗之，追至失列門林，遂擒乃顏。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the place of Buligud Botaha, Nayiyan's army was said to number one hundred thousand. Yuwashi plunged into the formation and fought fiercely, again defeating them, pursued to Shiliemenlin, and thus captured Nayiyan.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued to Buligud Botaha, where Nayiyan reportedly had a hundred thousand men. Yuwashi charged into the enemy ranks, broke them again, chased them to Shiliemenlin, and captured Nayiyan.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，賜金帶、只孫、錢幣甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit and granted a gold belt, zhisun robes, and money very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his feat and gave him a gold belt, zhisun robes, and a lavish purse.

sentences.zh: 乃顏餘黨塔不歹、金家奴聚兵滅捏該，從大軍討平之。

translations.literal: Nayiyan's remnant followers Tabudai and Jinjianu gathered troops at Mieniegai; he followed the great army to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Nayiyan's lieutenants Tabudai and Jinjianu rallied at Mieniegai, and he joined the main force in crushing them.

sentences.zh: 既而哈丹復叛於曲連江，追擊其軍，渡河而遁。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hadan again rebelled at Qulian River; he pursued and struck his army, which crossed the river and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hadan rebelled again at Qulian River; Yuwashi pursued his army until it fled across the river.

sentences.zh: 又與海都將八憐、帖里哥歹、必里察等戰於亦必兒失必兒之地，戰屢捷。

translations.literal: He again fought at Yibiershibi'er against Kaidu's generals Balin, Tiligedai, Bilicha, and others, winning repeated victories in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought Kaidu's generals Balin, Tiligedai, and Bilicha at Yibiershibi'er and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 成宗時在潛邸，帝以海都連年犯邊，命出鎮金山，玉哇失率所部在行。

translations.literal: When Chengzong was in the hidden residence, the emperor because Kaidu year after year violated the border ordered him to go out and garrison Jinshan; Yuwashi led his division on the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: While Chengzong was still heir apparent, Kublai sent him to garrison Jinshan against Kaidu's yearly raids, and Yuwashi marched with his troops.

sentences.zh: 從皇子闊闊出、丞相朶兒朶懷擊海都軍，突陣而入，大破之。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Kuokuchu and Chancellor Duoduhuai in striking Kaidu's army, burst through the formation, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Kuokuchu and Chancellor Duoduhuai he smashed through Kaidu's lines and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 復從諸王藥木忽兒、丞相朶兒朶懷擊海都將八憐，八憐敗。

translations.literal: He again followed Prince Yeshmutu'er and Chancellor Duoduhuai in striking Kaidu's general Balin; Balin was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Prince Yeshmutu'er and Duoduhuai against Kaidu's general Balin and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 海都復以禿苦馬領精兵三萬人直趨撒剌思河，欲據險以襲我師。

translations.literal: Kaidu again had Tuquma lead thirty thousand elite troops straight toward the Salasi River, intending to seize difficult ground to ambush our army.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidu sent Tuquma with thirty thousand picked men toward the Salasi River to seize the defiles and ambush the imperial force.

sentences.zh: 玉哇失率善射者三百人守其隘，注矢以射，竟全軍而歸。

translations.literal: Yuwashi led three hundred skilled archers to guard the pass, poured arrows in shooting, and finally brought the whole army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwashi held the pass with three hundred archers, rained arrows on the enemy, and brought the whole army back intact.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，賜鈔萬五千緡、金織段三十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and granted fifteen thousand strings of paper money and thirty bolts of gold-woven brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and gave him fifteen thousand strings of paper money and thirty bolts of gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 海都、朶哇以兵來襲，擊走之。

translations.literal: Kaidu and Duowa came with troops to attack; he struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaidu and Duowa attacked, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 武宗鎮北邊，海都復入寇，至兀兒禿，玉哇失敗之，獲其駝馬器仗以獻。

translations.literal: When Wuzong garrisoned the northern border, Kaidu again invaded to Wuerdu. Yuwashi defeated him and presented the camels, horses, and weapons captured.
translations.idiomatic: While Wuzong held the northern frontier, Kaidu raided again as far as Wuerdu. Yuwashi defeated him and presented the captured camels, horses, and arms.

sentences.zh: 時扎魯花赤孛羅帖木兒所將兵為海都困於小谷，帝命玉哇失援出之。

translations.literal: At that time the darughachi Boluotiemur's troops were trapped by Kaidu in a small valley; the emperor ordered Yuwashi to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Kaidu had trapped the darughachi Boluotiemur's men in a narrow valley, and the emperor sent Yuwashi to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，謂諸將曰：「今日大丈夫之事，舍玉哇失其誰能之，縱以黃金包其身，猶未足以厭朕志。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said to the generals: "For a great man's deeds today, apart from Yuwashi who could accomplish them? Even if gold wrapped his body, it would still not suffice to satisfy my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor told his generals, "Who but Yuwashi could do what a true man must do today? Even if I wrapped him in gold it would not repay what I owe him."

sentences.zh: 」武宗南還，命玉哇失後從，敵懼莫敢近，因留之戍邊。

translations.literal: When Wuzong returned south, he ordered Yuwashi to follow in the rear; the enemy feared and dared not approach, and so he was left to garrison the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong marched south he put Yuwashi in the rearguard; the enemy dared not come near, and Yuwashi was left to hold the frontier.

sentences.zh: 賜以金察剌二，玉束帶、渾金段各一，仍賜秫米七十石，使為酒以犒其軍。

translations.literal: He was granted two gold chasala ornaments, one jade belt set, one bolt of pure gold brocade, and also seventy shi of millet to make wine to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: He received two gold chasala ornaments, a jade belt set, a bolt of pure gold brocade, and seventy shi of grain to brew wine for his troops.

sentences.zh: 後海都子察八兒等遣人詣闕請和，朝廷許之，遂撤邊備，玉哇失乃還。

translations.literal: Later Kaidu's son Chabar and others sent men to the court requesting peace; the court consented, border defenses were then withdrawn, and Yuwashi returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kaidu's son Chabar sued for peace, the court agreed, the frontier garrisons were drawn down, and Yuwashi came home.

sentences.zh: 帝錄其功，賜鈔五萬貫，進鎮國上將軍，仍舊職。

translations.literal: The emperor recorded his merit, granted fifty thousand strings of paper money, advanced him to General for Stabilizing the State, and retained his former office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recorded his service, gave him fifty thousand strings of paper money, promoted him to general for stabilizing the state, and kept him in his old post.

sentences.zh: 大德十年五月，晝寢于衛舍，不疾而卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the tenth year of Dade he napped by day in the guard quarters and died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Dade 10 he fell asleep in the guard quarters at midday and died without warning.

sentences.zh: 子亦乞里歹襲。

translations.literal: His son Yiqilidai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiqilidai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 亦乞里歹卒，子拜住襲。

translations.literal: Yiqilidai died; his son Baizhu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiqilidai died, his son Baizhu took the post.

sentences.zh: 麥里，徹兀臺氏。

translations.literal: Maili was of the Che'utai clan.
translations.idiomatic: Maili belonged to the Che'utai clan.

sentences.zh: 祖雪里堅那顏，從太祖與王罕戰，同飲班真河水，以功授千戶，領徹里臺部，征討諸國，卒于河西。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sherijian Nayen followed Taizu in fighting Wang Han, drank together the waters of the Banzhen River, was for merit appointed chiliarch, led the Cheritai tribe, campaigned against the various states, and died in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sherijian Nayen fought Wang Han with Genghis Khan and drank from the Banzhen River with him. For his service he became a chiliarch leading the Cheritai and campaigned across many lands before dying in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 父麥吉襲職，從太宗定中原，以疾卒。

translations.literal: His father Maiji inherited the office, followed Taizong in pacifying the Central Plains, and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maiji inherited the post, helped Taizong pacify the Central Plains, and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 麥里襲職，從定宗略定欽察、阿速、斡魯思諸國。

translations.literal: Maili inherited the office and followed Dingzong in broadly pacifying the states of Qincha, Asud, and Oros.
translations.idiomatic: Maili inherited in turn and followed Dingzong in subduing Qincha, the Asud lands, and Oros.

sentences.zh: 從憲宗伐宋，有功。

translations.literal: He followed Xianzong in attacking the Song and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also served Xianzong against the Song with distinction.

sentences.zh: 探馬赤

translations.literal: Tanmachi
translations.idiomatic: Tanmachi

sentences.zh: 探馬赤，禿立不帶人。

translations.literal: Tanmachi was a man of Tulibudai.
translations.idiomatic: Tanmachi was of the Tulibudai people.

sentences.zh: 從諸王沒赤征蜀，後以兵從塔海紺卜、火魯赤、紐璘諸大帥。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Mechi in campaigning against Shu, and afterward served with troops under the great marshals Tahai Ganbu, Huoluchi, and Niulian.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Shu under Prince Mechi, then served under the great marshals Tahai Ganbu, Huoluchi, and Niulian.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，紐璘攻涪州，還至馬湖江，宋兵連艦絕江不得進，探馬赤率精兵二千擊之，奪其舟以濟。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu Niulian attacked Fuzhou. Returning to the Mahu River, Song troops linked warships to block the river and he could not advance. Tanmachi led two thousand elite troops to strike them, seized their boats to cross.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year Niulian attacked Fuzhou. On the return march at the Mahu River, Song warships blocked the crossing. Tanmachi led two thousand picked men, seized their boats, and forced a passage.

sentences.zh: 又於橫江、嘉定、宣化三縣造浮橋，以達成都，紐璘以為能，命將千人，從萬戶昔力荅略地碉門、黎、雅、土蕃。

translations.literal: He also built pontoon bridges at Hengjiang, Jiading, and Xuanhua counties to reach Chengdu. Niulian considered him capable and ordered him to command a thousand men, following Myriarch Xilida in seizing territory at Diaomen, Li, Ya, and the Tibetan regions.
translations.idiomatic: He also built pontoon bridges at Hengjiang, Jiading, and Xuanhua to open the route to Chengdu. Niulian judged him capable and gave him a thousand men under Myriarch Xilida to seize Diaomen, Li, Ya, and the Tibetan marches.

sentences.zh: 昔力荅死，行院帖赤以探馬赤為萬戶，領其軍。

translations.literal: When Xilida died, the mobile secretariat Tiechi made Tanmachi a myriarch to command his army.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilida died, the mobile secretariat Tiechi made Tanmachi a myriarch and gave him command of the force.

sentences.zh: 中統四年，授蒙古漢軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong he was appointed myriarch of the Mongol and Han army.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 4 he was made myriarch of the Mongol and Han army.

sentences.zh: 至元九年，從行省也速帶兒征建都，獨以銳卒千五百人，與建都兵戰于梅子嶺，大敗之，夜馳與速哥會，直擣其營，斬首數十級，生擒百餘人，獲其輜重以歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhiyuan he followed the provincial administration Yesudai'er in campaigning against Jiandu. Alone with fifteen hundred elite troops he fought Jiandu forces at Meizi Ridge and greatly defeated them. Riding through the night he joined Suge, struck straight at their camp, beheaded several tens, captured alive more than a hundred, and returned with their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 9 he joined Provincial Commissioner Yesudai'er against Jiandu with fifteen hundred picked men, routed the enemy at Meizi Ridge, rode through the night to join Suge, stormed their camp, took dozens of heads and more than a hundred prisoners, and returned with their baggage.

sentences.zh: 復益兵三千人，與左丞曲立吉思乘勝進擊，建都勢蹙，請降。

translations.literal: Three thousand more troops were added; with Left Chancellor Qulijisi he pressed the attack on the momentum of victory. Jiandu's situation grew tight and they requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforced by three thousand men, he and Left Chancellor Qulijisi pressed the victory until Jiandu, hard pressed, sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 又從行院汪田哥、忽敦等，攻嘉定、重慶、瀘、敘諸州，以功兼崇慶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He again followed the mobile secretariats Wang Tiange, Hudun, and others in attacking the prefectures of Jiading, Chongqing, Lu, and Xu. For his merit he was concurrently made darughachi of Chongqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought under Wang Tiange, Hudun, and others at Jiading, Chongqing, Lu, and Xu, and for his service was made concurrent darughachi of Chongqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the nineteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子拜延，襲蒙古軍萬戶，戍甘州。

translations.literal: His son Baiyan inherited as myriarch of the Mongol army and garrisoned Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baiyan inherited the Mongol myriarchy and was posted to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 拔都兒

translations.literal: Badou'er
translations.idiomatic: Badou'er

sentences.zh: 拔都兒，阿速氏，世居上都宜興。

translations.literal: Badou'er was of the Asud clan and for generations dwelt at Yixing in Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Badou'er was an Asud whose family had long lived at Yixing in Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在潛邸，與兄兀作兒不罕及馬塔兒沙帥衆來歸。

translations.literal: When Xianzong was in the hidden residence, he and his elder brother Wuzuo'erbohan and Mata'ersha led their multitude to submit.
translations.idiomatic: While Xianzong was still heir apparent, he came in with his elder brother Wuzuo'erbohan and Mata'ersha at the head of their people.

sentences.zh: 馬塔兒沙從憲宗征麥各思城，為前鋒將，身中二矢，奮戰拔其城。

translations.literal: Mata'ersha followed Xianzong in campaigning against Maigesicheng as vanguard general, was struck by two arrows in the body, fought fiercely, and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: Mata'ersha marched with Xianzong against Maigesicheng as vanguard, took two arrows, and still stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 又從征蜀，至釣魚山，歿于軍。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Shu, reached Diaoyushan, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He later campaigned in Shu as far as Diaoyushan and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 拔都兒從征李璮，圍濟南，身二十餘戰，世祖嘉其能，賞納失思段九，命領阿速軍一千，常居左右。

translations.literal: Badou'er followed the campaign against Li Tan, besieged Jinan, and personally fought in more than twenty battles. Emperor Shizu praised his ability, rewarded nine bolts of nashisi brocade, ordered him to command a thousand Asud troops, and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Badou'er joined the campaign against Li Tan and fought more than twenty times at the siege of Jinan. Kublai admired his skill, gave him nine bolts of nashisi brocade, put a thousand Asud troops under him, and kept him close at hand.

sentences.zh: 尋於阿塔赤內充怯薛百戶。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served within Atachi's guard as a keshig centurion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a keshig centurion in Atachi's guard.

sentences.zh: 後從塔不台南征，與敵軍戰于金剛臺，又以功受賞。

translations.literal: Later he followed Tabutai on the southern campaign, fought the enemy army at the Jingang Platform, and again received reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He later marched south with Tabutai, fought at the Jingang Platform, and was rewarded again.

sentences.zh: 師還，言於帝曰：「臣願從軍，為國效死。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he said to the emperor: "Your subject wishes to follow the army and die in service to the state."
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he told the emperor, "I wish to stay with the troops and give my life for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」世祖留之，仍命充孛可孫，兼領阿速軍，御馬必令鞚引。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu kept him, still ordered him to serve as bekson, concurrently commanded the Asud army, and whenever the imperial horse went out always had him hold the bridle and lead.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai kept him at court as bekson, still in command of the Asud troops, and always had him lead the imperial horse by the bridle.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒

translations.literal: Angji'er
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒，張掖人，姓野蒲氏，世為西夏將家。

translations.literal: Angji'er was a man of Zhangye, surname Yepu, for generations a military family of Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er came from Zhangye, bore the surname Yepu, and his family had been generals of Western Xia for generations.

sentences.zh: 歲辛巳，父甘卜率所部歸太祖，以其軍隸蒙古軍籍，仍以甘卜為千戶主之。

translations.literal: In the year xinsi his father Ganbu led his division to submit to Taizu. His army was placed on the Mongol military register, and Ganbu was still made chiliarch to command it.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year his father Ganbu brought his men to Genghis Khan, enrolled them in the Mongol army rolls, and remained their chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎出征，病卒。

translations.literal: He followed Muqali on campaign and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Muqali and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒領其父軍，從征諸國有功。

translations.literal: Angji'er took his father's army and followed campaigns against the various states with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er took over his father's troops and won credit on campaigns across many lands.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，授本軍千戶，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed chiliarch of his own army, wearing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6 he became chiliarch of his own unit with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 俄略地淮南，所向無前。

translations.literal: Soon he seized territory south of the Huai; wherever he went none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon swept south of the Huai and met no equal.

sentences.zh: 時國兵初南，塞馬當暑，往往疥癘，昂吉兒以所部馬入太行療之，所病良已。

translations.literal: At that time the national army had just gone south; frontier horses in midsummer often suffered scab and mange. Angji'er took his division's horses into the Taihang to treat them, and those that were ill all recovered well.
translations.idiomatic: As the army first marched south, northern horses sickened in the summer heat with mange and scab. Angji'er sent his horses into the Taihang to recover, and they healed.

sentences.zh: 由是軍中馬病者，率以屬焉，歲療馬以萬數。

translations.literal: From this, sick horses in the army generally were entrusted to him; each year he treated horses by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After that, sick army horses were routinely sent to him, and he treated tens of thousands each year.

sentences.zh: 宋輸糧金剛臺，意將深入，昂吉兒將兵馳往，斷其輸道，因上言：「河南邊郡與宋對境，宋兵時為邊患，唐州東南皆大山，信陽在蔡州南，南直九里、武陽、平靖、五水等關，宋兵必經諸關以入，信陽實其咽喉，守禦莫急焉。

translations.literal: The Song were transporting grain to the Jingang Platform, intending to advance deeply. Angji'er led troops in rapid march, cut their supply route, and therefore memorialized: "The border commanderies of Henan face the Song frontier, and Song troops often become border troubles. Southeast of Tangzhou are all great mountains. Xinyang lies south of Caizhou; south of it lie directly the passes of Jiuli, Wuyang, Pingjing, Wushui, and others. Song troops must pass these passes to enter; Xinyang is truly their throat—there is nothing more urgent than to defend it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Song sent grain to the Jingang Platform for a deeper push, Angji'er raced to cut their supply line and memorialized the throne: "Henan's border counties face Song territory and suffer constant raids. Southeast of Tangzhou lies rugged mountain country. Xinyang sits south of Caizhou on the road to the passes of Jiuli, Wuyang, Pingjing, and Wushui—any Song advance must come that way. Xinyang is the choke point and must be held first."

sentences.zh: 往年金亡，朝廷得壽、泗、襄、郢，而不留兵守，卒使宋得之，請城信陽，以扼宋。

translations.literal: In former years when Jin perished, the court took Shou, Si, Xiang, and Ying but did not leave troops to guard them, and in the end allowed the Song to take them. I request to fortify Xinyang to choke the Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin fell we took Shou, Si, Xiang, and Ying but left no garrison, and the Song seized them. I ask that Xinyang be fortified to block the Song advance.

sentences.zh: 」得旨，令率河西軍一千三百人城之，城成。

translations.literal: He received the edict and was ordered to lead thirteen hundred Hexi troops to build the city; the city was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered him to build the city with thirteen hundred Hexi troops; the work was finished.

sentences.zh: 九年，加明威將軍、信陽軍萬戶，佩虎符，分木華黎及阿朮所將河西兵俾將之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was advanced to General of Illustrious Might and myriarch of Xinyang Army, wearing a tiger tally; the Hexi troops formerly led by Muqali and Azhu were divided and given him to command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became general of illustrious might and myriarch of Xinyang Army with a tiger tally, commanding the Hexi troops once led by Muqali and Azhu.

sentences.zh: 加懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General for Cherishing the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general for cherishing the distant.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏渡江，留阿朮定淮南東道，其西道則屬之昂吉兒，駐兵和州。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan crossed the Yangtze, Azhu was left to pacify the eastern route of Huainan; the western route was placed under Angji'er, who encamped at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan crossed the Yangtze, Azhu held eastern Huainan while Angji'er took the western route and camped at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 宋淮西制置夏貴遣侯都統將兵四萬來攻，有謀內應者悉誅之，潛兵出千秋澗，塞其歸路，因出城奮擊，大敗之，獲人馬千計。

translations.literal: Song Huaixi commissioner Xia Gui dispatched Commander Hou with forty thousand troops to attack. Those plotting internal collusion were all executed. He secretly sent troops out through Qianqiu Ravine to block their retreat, then sallied from the city and struck fiercely, greatly defeating them and capturing men and horses by the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Song Huaixi commissioner Xia Gui sent Commander Hou with forty thousand men. Angji'er executed would-be collaborators, sent a hidden force through Qianqiu Ravine to cut the enemy's retreat, sallied from the city, and routed them, taking thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 鎮巢軍降，阿速軍戍之，人不堪其橫，都統洪福盡殺戍者以叛。

translations.literal: Zhenchao Army surrendered; Asud troops garrisoned it. The people could not bear their brutality; Commander Hong Fu killed all the garrison troops and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenchao surrendered, Asud troops garrisoned it until the people could bear their abuses no longer. Commander Hong Fu slaughtered the garrison and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒攻拔其城，擒福及董統制、譚正將。

translations.literal: Angji'er attacked and captured the city, seizing Fu and Commissioners Dong and Tan Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er stormed the city and captured Hong Fu along with Commissioners Dong and Tan Zheng.

sentences.zh: 遂攻廬州，夏貴使人來言曰：「公毋吾攻為也，吾主降，吾即降矣。

translations.literal: He then attacked Luzhou. Xia Gui sent a messenger saying: "Sir, do not attack me. When my lord surrenders, I shall surrender at once."
translations.idiomatic: He then moved on Luzhou. Xia Gui sent word: "Do not press me—once my sovereign surrenders, I shall surrender at once."

sentences.zh: 」宋亡，貴舉所部納款。

translations.literal: When the Song perished, Gui brought his entire command to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell, Xia Gui brought his whole command over.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒入廬州，民按堵無所犯，遷鎮國上將軍、淮西宣慰使。

translations.literal: Angji'er entered Luzhou; the people were secure and he violated nothing. He was transferred to General for Stabilizing the State and Huaixi pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er entered Luzhou without harming the people and was promoted to general for stabilizing the state and Huaixi pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宋丞相文天祥復起兵海道，舒民張德興應之，襲破興國、德安諸郡，還據司空山。

translations.literal: Song Chancellor Wen Tianxiang again raised troops by the sea route; Shuzhou man Zhang Dexing responded, raided and captured the prefectures of Xingguo and De'an, and returned to hold Sikong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Song chancellor Wen Tianxiang rallied forces along the coast; Zhang Dexing of Shuzhou joined him, seized Xingguo and De'an, and held Sikong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 詔昂吉兒攻之，一戰而定，殺張德興，執其三子以獻。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Angji'er to attack them; one battle settled it. He killed Zhang Dexing and seized his three sons to present.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Angji'er against them; one battle ended the revolt. He killed Zhang Dexing and sent his three sons to the capital.

sentences.zh: 江左初平，官制草創，權臣阿合馬納賂鬻爵，江南官僚冗濫為甚，郡守而下佩金符者多至三四人，由行省官舉薦超授宣慰使者甚衆，民不堪命。

translations.literal: When the lower Yangtze was first pacified, the official system was newly created. The powerful minister Ahmad took bribes to sell offices; bureaucrats south of the Yangtze were redundantly excessive. Below prefects, those wearing gold tallies often reached three or four per post. Many were promoted beyond their qualifications to pacification commissioner through recommendations by provincial officials; the people could not bear the burdens.
translations.idiomatic: After the lower Yangtze was pacified, offices were still being invented and Ahmad sold posts for bribes. Jiangnan was awash in redundant officials—some counties had three or four men with gold tallies—and provincial patrons pushed unqualified men into pacification posts until the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒入朝，具為帝言之，且枚舉不循資歷而驟陞者數人。

translations.literal: Angji'er entered court and reported all this fully to the emperor, and also enumerated by name several who had been suddenly promoted without following seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er came to court, laid the whole matter before the emperor, and named several men promoted far beyond their rank.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「有是哉！

translations.literal: The emperor said in alarm: "So it is!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Can this be true?"

sentences.zh: 」因謂姚樞等曰：「此卿輩所知，而不為朕言，昂吉兒顧言之邪。

translations.literal: He then said to Yao Shu and others: "This is what you gentlemen know, yet you did not speak to Us—only Angji'er troubled to say it?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Yao Shu and the others and said, "You knew this and never told me—only Angji'er would speak up?"

sentences.zh: 」即命偕平章哈伯、左丞崔斌、翰林承旨和魯火孫、符寶奉御董文忠減汰之，選曹以清。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them together with Pacification Commissioner Habo, Left Chancellor Cui Bin, Hanlin Academician Heluohuosun, and Imperial Insignia Attendant Dong Wenzong to reduce and eliminate redundant posts; the selection offices thereby became clear.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered Habo, Cui Bin, Heluohuosun, and Dong Wenzong to weed out the excess, and the personnel offices were cleared.

sentences.zh: 仍詔諭江淮軍民，俾通知之。

translations.literal: An edict was still issued to proclaim this to the armies and people of the Jianghuai region so they would know of it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also announced the purge to the armies and people of the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 時兩淮兵革之餘，荊榛蔽野，昂吉兒請立屯田，以給軍餉，帝從之。

translations.literal: At that time, after warfare in the two Huai regions, brambles and thorns covered the fields. Angji'er requested to establish military colonies to supply army provisions; the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars on the two Huai, the fields lay waste under thorn and bramble. Angji'er asked to establish military colonies to feed the troops, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 既而阿塔海言：「屯田所用人牛農具甚衆，今方有事日本，若復調發民兵，將不勝動搖矣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Atahai said: "Military colonies require very many men, oxen, and farm tools. Now there is business with Japan; if militia are again mobilized, the people will not be able to bear the disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: Atahai then objected: "Colonies need vast numbers of men, oxen, and tools. We are already committed against Japan; another levy would shake the realm."

sentences.zh: 」議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宣慰使燕公楠復以為言，帝乃遣數千人，即芍陂、洪澤試之，果如昂吉兒所言，乃以二萬兵屯之，歲得米數十萬斛。

translations.literal: Before long Pacification Commissioner Yan Gongnan again spoke on the matter. The emperor then sent several thousand men to try it at Shaopi and Hongze; it turned out just as Angji'er had said. He then stationed twenty thousand troops there, and each year obtained several hundred thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Pacification Commissioner Yan Gongnan raised it again. The emperor sent several thousand men to trial plots at Shaopi and Hongze, and the yield matched Angji'er's prediction. Twenty thousand colonists were posted there, producing hundreds of thousands of hu of rice each year.

sentences.zh: 加輔國上將軍、河南行省參知政事、淮西宣慰使都元帥，進驃騎衛上將軍、行中書省左丞，加龍虎衛上將軍、行尚書省右丞，兩官皆兼淮西使、帥。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General for Assisting the State, Associate Administrative Commissioner of the Henan Branch Secretariat, and Grand Marshal of the Huaixi Pacification Commissioner; promoted to General of the Biaoqi Guard, Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat; and added General of the Longhu Guard and Right Chancellor of the Branch Ministry—both posts concurrently holding Huaixi commissioner and commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general for assisting the state, Henan associate commissioner, and Huaixi grand marshal, then became biaoqi guard general and branch secretariat left chancellor, and also longhu guard general and branch ministry right chancellor, retaining Huaixi civil and military command throughout.

sentences.zh: 日本不庭，帝命阿塔海等領卒十萬征之。

translations.literal: Japan was insubordinate; the emperor ordered Atahai and others to lead a hundred thousand troops to campaign against it.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan refused tribute, the emperor ordered Atahai and others to take a hundred thousand men against it.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒上疏，其略曰：「臣聞兵以氣為主，而上下同欲者勝。

translations.literal: Angji'er submitted a memorial, its gist saying: "Your subject has heard that in warfare morale is paramount, and where superiors and subordinates share the same desire, there is victory."
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er memorialized the throne in substance as follows: "I have heard that armies live on morale and win only when ruler and troops want the same thing."

sentences.zh: 比者連事外夷，三軍屢衂，不可以言氣，海內騷然，一遇調發，上下愁怨，非所謂同欲也，請罷兵息民。

translations.literal: Recently we have had continuous dealings with foreign barbarians; the three armies have repeatedly been defeated—one cannot speak of morale. Within the seas there is turmoil; whenever levies are issued, superiors and subordinates grieve and resent. This is not what is called sharing the same desire. I request to halt the armies and give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: Lately we have fought abroad again and again while the armies suffer defeat after defeat—there is no morale left. The realm is unsettled; every levy breeds resentment above and below. That is not shared purpose. I beg you to stop the campaigns and let the people rest."

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 既而師果無功。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the army indeed achieved no success.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition failed, as he had warned.

sentences.zh: 昂吉兒屢為直言，雖帝怒甚，其辭不少屈。

translations.literal: Angji'er repeatedly spoke blunt truth; even when the emperor was very angry, his words did not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Angji'er spoke blunt truth again and again, and even when the emperor flew into a rage he would not soften his words.

sentences.zh: 臺臣慮昂吉兒難制，以牙以迷失不畏強禦，奏為本道按察使以察之。

translations.literal: Censorate officials feared Angji'er was hard to control. Because Yayishimishi did not fear the powerful, they memorialized to make him surveillance commissioner of the circuit to investigate him.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate feared Angji'er was unmanageable and, because Yayishimishi was known not to flinch before the powerful, had him made circuit surveillance commissioner to watch him.

sentences.zh: 牙以迷失時捃摭昂吉兒細故以聞，及廷辨，帝察其無他，輒遷其官，後竟以微過罪之。

translations.literal: Yayishimishi from time to time gathered Angji'er's minor matters to report. When they argued at court, the emperor saw he had no other intent and repeatedly transferred his office; in the end he was punished for a slight fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yayishimishi kept reporting petty complaints against Angji'er. At court the emperor saw no malice and kept shifting Yayishimishi's post, but in the end punished him for a trifling offense.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yuanzhen 1.

sentences.zh: 子五人，其顯者曰昂阿禿，廬州蒙古漢軍萬戶府達魯花赤；

translations.literal: He had five sons; among the prominent were Ang'atu, darughachi of the Luzhou Mongol and Han Army Myriarchate;
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. The notable ones were Ang'atu, darughachi of the Luzhou Mongol and Han myriarchate;

sentences.zh: 曰暗普，海北海南道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: and Anpu, surveillance commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit for rectifying government and investigating corruption.
translations.idiomatic: and Anpu, surveillance commissioner of the Haibei and Hainan circuit.

sentences.zh: 孫教化的，世襲千戶。

translations.literal: His grandson Jiaohuade inherited the chiliarchy by generations.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Jiaohuade inherited the chiliarchy in the family line.

sentences.zh: 哈剌，哈魯氏。

translations.literal: Hala was of the Halu clan.
translations.idiomatic: Hala belonged to the Halu clan.

sentences.zh: 初從軍攻襄樊，蒙古四萬戶府辟為水軍鎮撫。

translations.literal: At first he followed the army in attacking Xiangyang and Fancheng; the Mongol Fourth Myriarchate recruited him as naval regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first campaigned at Xiangyang and Fancheng and was recruited by the Fourth Mongol Myriarchate as naval regional commander.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，從丞相伯顏渡江，改管軍百戶，賞甲冑、銀鞘刀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan he followed Chancellor Bayan in crossing the Yangtze, was changed to centurion in charge of troops, and rewarded with armor and a silver-sheathed knife.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 12 he crossed the Yangtze with Bayan, became a troop centurion, and received armor and a silver-sheathed knife.

sentences.zh: 十二年秋，從丞相阿朮與宋兵戰焦山，敗之，獲海舟二。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twelfth year he followed Chancellor Azhu in fighting Song troops at Jiaoshan, defeated them, and captured two seagoing vessels.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he fought the Song with Azhu at Jiaoshan, routed them, and took two seagoing vessels.

sentences.zh: 阿朮與王世強招討造白鷂海船百艘，就四十一萬戶翼摘遣漢軍三千五百、新附軍一千五百，俾哈剌、王世強并統之。

translations.literal: Azhu and Wang Shiqiang, pacification commissioners, built a hundred white-hawk seagoing ships. From the wing of the Forty-first Myriarchate they selected and dispatched thirty-five hundred Han troops and fifteen hundred newly attached troops, making Hala and Wang Shiqiang jointly command them.
translations.idiomatic: Azhu and Pacification Commissioner Wang Shiqiang built a hundred white-hawk warships, drew thirty-five hundred Han and fifteen hundred newly attached troops from the Forty-first Myriarchate wing, and put Hala and Wang Shiqiang in joint command.

sentences.zh: 攻宋江陰、許浦、金山、上海、崇明、金浦皆下之，獲海船三百餘艘，遂戍澉浦海口。

translations.literal: Attacking Song Jiangyin, Xupu, Jinshan, Shanghai, Chongming, and Jinpu, he captured them all, obtained more than three hundred seagoing vessels, and then garrisoned the seaport of Ganpu.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiangyin, Xupu, Jinshan, Shanghai, Chongming, and Jinpu, seized more than three hundred warships, and garrisoned the Ganpu estuary.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，行省檄充沿海招討副使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year the provincial administration ordered him to serve as associate coastal pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year the provincial administration named him associate coastal pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宋將張世傑舟師至慶元朐山東門海界，哈剌追之，獲船四艘，上其功，行省增撥軍七百并舊所領士卒，守定海港口。

translations.literal: Song general Zhang Shijie's fleet reached the sea boundary east of Qushan Gate in Qingyuan. Hala pursued them, captured four vessels, reported his merit, and the provincial administration added seven hundred troops to his former command to guard Dinghai Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shijie's fleet reached the sea off eastern Qushan in Qingyuan, Hala pursued, took four ships, reported his success, and was reinforced with seven hundred men to hold Dinghai Harbor.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，宋昌國州、朐山、秀山戍兵舟師千餘艘，攻奪定海港口，哈剌迎擊，虜其裨將并海船三艘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, more than a thousand Song warships from the garrisons of Changguo Prefecture, Qushan, and Xiushan attacked and seized Dinghai Harbor. Hala met the attack, captured their deputy general and three seagoing vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month more than a thousand Song ships from Changguo, Qushan, and Xiushan seized Dinghai Harbor. Hala counterattacked and captured a deputy commander and three warships.

sentences.zh: 八月，宋兵復攻定海港口，哈剌擊退之，行省檄充蒙古漢軍招討使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Song troops again attacked Dinghai Harbor; Hala beat them back. The provincial administration ordered him to serve as Mongol and Han pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Song attacked Dinghai again and Hala drove them off. The provincial administration then named him Mongol and Han pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十月，哈剌引兵至溫州青門，遇宋兵，奪船五艘，遣使諭溫州守臣家之柄以城降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Hala led troops to Qing'ao Gate in Wenzhou, met Song troops, seized five vessels, and sent a messenger to instruct Wenzhou defender Jia Zhibing to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Hala reached Qing'ao Gate in Wenzhou, met Song forces, took five ships, and sent word to the defender Jia Zhibing to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月，至福州，奪宋海船二十艘，擒毛監丞等。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he reached Fuzhou, seized twenty Song seagoing vessels, and captured Supervisor Mao and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he reached Fuzhou, took twenty Song warships, and captured Supervisor Mao and others.

sentences.zh: 十四年，賜金符，宣武將軍、沿海招討副使，行省檄充沿海經略副使，俾與劉萬戶行元帥府事於慶元，鎮守沿海上下，南至福建，北趾許浦。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was granted a gold tally, made General of Martial Proclamation and associate coastal pacification commissioner. The provincial administration ordered him to serve as associate coastal commissioner-in-chief, and had him with Myriarch Liu conduct marshal headquarters affairs at Qingyuan, garrisoning the coast from Fujian in the south to Xupu in the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received a gold tally as general of martial proclamation and associate coastal pacification commissioner, then became associate coastal commissioner-in-chief. With Myriarch Liu he ran the marshal's headquarters at Qingyuan, guarding the coast from Fujian south to Xupu north.

sentences.zh: 六月，行省檄充沿海經略使，兼左副都元帥，督造海船千艘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the provincial administration ordered him to serve as coastal commissioner-in-chief, concurrently left associate grand marshal, supervising the construction of a thousand seagoing ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was named coastal commissioner-in-chief and left associate grand marshal and ordered to build a thousand warships.

sentences.zh: 八月，有旨：江西省右丞塔出等進兵攻廣南，哈剌以兵從。

translations.literal: In the eighth month there was an edict: Jiangxi Branch Secretariat Right Chancellor Tachu and others were to advance troops to attack Guangnan; Hala followed with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ordered Jiangxi right chancellor Tachu and others against Guangnan, and Hala marched with them.

sentences.zh: 十月，進昭勇大將軍、沿海招討使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was advanced to General of Martial Valor and coastal pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to general of martial valor and coastal pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時宋處州兵復溫州，哈剌歹率兵復取之。

translations.literal: At that time Song troops from Chuzhou recovered Wenzhou; Haladai led troops and recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces from Chuzhou had retaken Wenzhou, and Haladai marched in and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 進至潮陽縣，宋都統陳懿等兄弟五人以畬兵七千人降。

translations.literal: Advancing to Chaoyang County, Song Commander Chen Yi and his five brothers with seven thousand She troops surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Chaoyang County, Song commander Chen Yi and his five brothers surrendered with seven thousand She troops.

sentences.zh: 塔出兵攻廣州，踰月未下，哈剌引兵繼至，諭宋安撫張鎮孫、侍郎譚應斗以城降。

translations.literal: Tachu's army attacked Guangzhou; for more than a month it would not fall. Hala led troops in succession and instructed Song Pacification Commissioner Zhang Zhensun and Vice Minister Tan Yingdou to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tachu besieged Guangzhou for more than a month without success. Hala came up behind and persuaded pacification commissioner Zhang Zhensun and vice minister Tan Yingdou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 從攻張世傑于大洋，獲其軍資器械不可勝計。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking Zhang Shijie on the great ocean and obtained his military stores and weapons beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attack on Zhang Shijie at sea and captured stores and arms beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 諭南恩州，宋閤門宣贊、舍人梁國傑以畬軍萬人降。

translations.literal: He instructed Nan'en Prefecture; Song Gate Proclaimer Liang Guojie with ten thousand She troops surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Nan'en Prefecture, Song gate proclaimer Liang Guojie surrendered with ten thousand She troops.

sentences.zh: 十五年，還軍慶元。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the army returned to Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the army returned to Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，入覲，帝問曰：「汝何氏族？

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn he entered audience. The emperor asked: "Of what clan and surname are you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he presented himself at court. The emperor asked, "What is your clan?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣哈魯人。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject is a Halu man."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am a Halu man, Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」賜金織文衣、鞍勒，擢昭武大將軍、沿海左副都元帥、慶元路緫管府達魯花赤，將所部軍戍海口。

translations.literal: He was granted gold-woven ceremonial robes and saddle trappings, promoted to General of Martial Solemnity, left associate coastal grand marshal, and darughachi of the Qingyuan Circuit General Administration, leading his division to garrison the seaport.
translations.idiomatic: He received gold-woven robes and saddle gear, was made general of martial solemnity, left associate coastal grand marshal, and Qingyuan circuit darughachi, and garrisoned the seaport with his troops.

sentences.zh: 十六年，日本商船四艘，篙師二千餘人至慶元港口，哈剌歹諜知其無他，言于行省，與交易而遣之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year four Japanese merchant ships with more than two thousand boatmen reached Qingyuan Harbor. Haladai spied and knew they had no other intent, reported to the provincial administration, traded with them, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year four Japanese merchant ships with more than two thousand crew reached Qingyuan. Haladai found they meant no harm, reported to the provincial administration, traded with them, and sent them on.

sentences.zh: 海賊賀文達、顧潤等寇掠海島，哈剌歹諭降之，得舟六十餘艘。

translations.literal: Sea bandits He Wenda, Gu Run, and others raided coastal islands. Haladai instructed them to surrender and obtained more than sixty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits He Wenda, Gu Run, and others raided the islands until Haladai talked them into surrender and took more than sixty ships.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢輔國上將軍、都元帥，從國兵征日本，值颶風，舟回。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was advanced to General for Assisting the State and grand marshal, followed the national army in campaigning against Japan, met a typhoon, and the ships returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became general for assisting the state and grand marshal, joined the invasion of Japan, and turned back when a typhoon struck the fleet.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，還戍慶元。

translations.literal: In the second month of the next year he returned to garrison Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month he returned to garrison Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，罷都元帥，改沿海上萬戶府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the post of grand marshal was abolished; he was changed to darughachi of the Coastal Superior Myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the grand marshal post was abolished and he became darughachi of the coastal superior myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入朝，帝問日本事宜，哈剌歹應對甚悉，令還戍海道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he entered court. The emperor asked about Japanese affairs; Haladai answered very fully and ordered him to return to garrison the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he came to court, answered the emperor's questions about Japan in detail, and was sent back to guard the sea routes.

sentences.zh: 授浙東宣慰使，賜金織文段、玉束帶、鞍勒、弓矢有差。

translations.literal: He was appointed Zhedong pacification commissioner and granted gold-woven brocade, jade belt set, saddle trappings, and bow and arrows in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Zhedong pacification commissioner and given gold brocade, a jade belt set, saddle gear, and bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，樞密以水軍乏帥，奏兼前職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Bureau of Military Affairs, because the navy lacked commanders, memorialized that he concurrently hold his former military post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year the Bureau of Military Affairs, citing a shortage of naval commanders, had him resume his former military post as well.

sentences.zh: 冬，徵入見。

translations.literal: In winter he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜金吾衛上將軍、中書左丞，行浙東道宣慰使，領軍職如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed General of the Jinyu Guard and Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, acting Zhedong Circuit pacification commissioner, retaining his military office as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became jinyu guard general and secretariat left chancellor, acting Zhedong pacification commissioner, while keeping his military command.

sentences.zh: 沙全，哈剌魯氏。

translations.literal: Sha Quan was of the Qarluq clan.
translations.idiomatic: Sha Quan belonged to the Qarluq clan.

sentences.zh: 父沙的，世居沙漠，從太祖平金，戍河南柳泉，家焉。

translations.literal: His father Shadi for generations dwelt in the desert, followed Taizu in pacifying Jin, garrisoned Liuchuan in Henan, and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shadi had long lived in the steppe, followed Genghis Khan in conquering Jin, and settled at Liuchuan in Henan on garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 全初名抄兒赤，甫五歲，為宋軍所虜，年十八，留劉整幕下，宋人以其父名沙的，使以沙為姓，而名曰全。

translations.literal: Quan was originally named Chao'erchi. At only five years he was captured by Song troops. At eighteen he remained under Liu Zheng's command. The Song, because his father's name was Shadi, made Sha his surname and called him Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was born Chao'erchi. The Song captured him at five, and at eighteen he served in Liu Zheng's staff. The Song took his father's name Shadi, gave him the surname Sha, and called him Quan.

sentences.zh: 全久居宋，險固備知之。

translations.literal: Quan had long dwelt in Song territory and knew all its defenses thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Having lived long under the Song, he knew every pass and strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，整以瀘州來歸，全與之同行，宋軍追之，全力戰得脫，授管軍百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Zheng came over with Luzhou; Quan went with him. Song troops pursued them; Quan fought with all his strength and escaped, and was appointed centurion in charge of troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 Zheng defected with Luzhou and Quan went with him. Pursued by Song forces, Quan fought his way clear and was made a troop centurion.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，整出兵雲頂山，與宋將夏貴兵遇，全擊殺甚衆。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, Zheng led troops out from Yunding Mountain and met the army of Song general Xia Gui; Quan struck and killed very many.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3 Zheng marched from Yunding Mountain, met Song general Xia Gui, and Quan killed a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 五年，命整領都元帥事，出師圍襄樊，以全為鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zheng was ordered to take charge of grand marshal affairs, led troops out to besiege Xiangyang and Fancheng, and Quan was made regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Zheng was put in charge of the grand marshal's command, besieged Xiangyang and Fancheng, and made Quan regional commander.

sentences.zh: 整遣全率軍攻仙人山、陳家洞諸寨，破之，陞千戶，賜銀符。

translations.literal: Zheng dispatched Quan to lead troops attacking the stockades of Xianren Mountain, Chenjiadong, and others, captured them, promoted him to chiliarch, and granted a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng sent Quan against the stockades at Xianren Mountain and Chenjiadong. After they fell he was promoted to chiliarch and given a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 敗宋將張貴，拔樊城，與劉整軍會。

translations.literal: He defeated Song general Zhang Gui, captured Fancheng, and joined Liu Zheng's army.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Song general Zhang Gui, took Fancheng, and rejoined Liu Zheng.

sentences.zh: 修正陽城，引兵渡淮，與宋將陳安撫戰，敗之。

translations.literal: He repaired Zhengyang city, led troops across the Huai, fought Song Pacification Commissioner Chen, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired Zhengyang, crossed the Huai, and defeated Song pacification commissioner Chen.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從丞相阿朮與宋將張世傑、孫虎臣大戰于焦山，水陸並進，宋人不能支，盡棄鼓旗走，獲其將士三十三人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed Chancellor Azhu in a great battle with Song generals Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen at Jiaoshan. Land and water advanced together; the Song could not withstand it, abandoned all drums and banners and fled, and thirty-three of their officers and soldiers were captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he fought with Azhu against Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen at Jiaoshan. The combined land and sea assault broke the Song line; they fled abandoning drums and banners, and thirty-three officers and men were taken.

sentences.zh: 從攻常州，克之，乘勝下沿海諸城。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Changzhou, captured it, and on the momentum of victory reduced the coastal cities.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Changzhou and then swept down the coastal cities in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 至華亭，戒士卒毋殺掠，遂傾城出降，以功授華亭軍民達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Reaching Huating, he warned the soldiers not to kill or plunder; the whole city then came out to surrender. For his merit he was appointed darughachi of Huating military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Huating he forbade killing and looting, and the whole city surrendered. For this he was made darughachi of Huating.

sentences.zh: 時民心未定，有未附鹽徒聚衆數萬掠華亭，全擊破之，籍其名得六千人，請于行省，遣屯田于淮之芍陂。

translations.literal: At that time popular sentiment was not yet settled; unaffiliated salt smugglers gathered tens of thousands and raided Huating. Quan struck and defeated them, registered their names and obtained six thousand men, requested the provincial administration, and sent them to military colonies at Shaopi on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unsettled when unaffiliated salt gangs of tens of thousands raided Huating. Quan defeated them, registered six thousand men, and asked the provincial administration to settle them at Shaopi on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 行省以邑人新附，時有叛側，委萬戶忽都忽等體察，欲屠其城，全言：「鹽卒多非其土人，若屠之，枉死者衆。

translations.literal: The provincial administration, because the townspeople were newly submitted and from time to time rebelled, entrusted Myriarch Huduhu and others to investigate and intended to slaughter the city. Quan said: "Most of the salt soldiers were not natives of this place; if the city is slaughtered, many will die unjustly."
translations.idiomatic: Because the town had only lately submitted and still wavered, the provincial administration sent Myriarch Huduhu to investigate and planned a massacre. Quan argued, "Most of the salt rebels were outsiders—a massacre would kill many innocents."

sentences.zh: 」以死保其不叛，遂止。

translations.literal: He pledged his life to guarantee they would not rebel, and the slaughter was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged his life that they would not rebel, and the massacre was called off.

sentences.zh: 賜金符，加武略將軍，兼領鹽場，職如舊。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold tally, advanced to General of Military Stratagem, and concurrently commanded the salt works, his office as before.
translations.idiomatic: He received a gold tally and promotion to general of military stratagem, still overseeing the salt works.

sentences.zh: 尋陞華亭為府，以全為達魯花赤，賜虎符。

translations.literal: Soon Huating was elevated to a prefecture; Quan was made its darughachi and granted a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Huating was soon raised to a prefecture, and Quan became its darughachi with a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂起，其最盛者有衆數千人，全悉招來之，境內得安。

translations.literal: At that time bandits swarmed up; the most powerful had forces of several thousand. Quan summoned them all to submit, and within the borders peace was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose everywhere, some with thousands of men. Quan talked them all into submission and restored order in the district.

sentences.zh: 改松江萬戶府達魯花赤，始專領軍政。
